idiom_name: match (a, b) over enum variants (exhaustive tag dispatch)
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance and no virtual double dispatch to fight: the idiomatic replacement is a closed enum whose match the compiler checks for exhaustiveness, and since match accepts tuple patterns one `match (a, b)` arm resolves both variants at once - a missing cell is a compile error, not a runtime default. This covers everything a visitor does for data you own; when the type set must stay open (types from other crates, plugin nodes) the trait-object visitor (see trait-object-visitor) or Any-based downcasting takes over and exhaustiveness is lost.
pitfalls: A trailing `_ =>` arm silently swallows newly added variants: enumerate the variants so adding one breaks the build.
Recursive variants need indirection (Box) and matching by reference (`match (&a, &b)`) to avoid moving the values.
Commutative pairs written out twice drift apart: canonicalise on the discriminant before matching.

variants.name: Trait-object visitor (open element set)
variants.idiom_name: trait Visitor { fn visit_circle(&mut self, &Circle); } + fn accept(&self, &mut dyn Visitor)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic structure translated literally onto trait objects: Element::accept takes &mut dyn Visitor and calls the per-type visit method, so the first dispatch goes through the vtable and the second is static overload resolution on the concrete receiver inside accept. It buys an open element set - any crate can implement the trait - and pays with lost exhaustiveness, extra indirection and Box allocation in heterogeneous collections; the provided-method pattern (a walk_* free function or a default visit that recurses, as in syn's Visit trait) factors a shared traversal out of the operations. Where the element set is closed, the enum form is strictly cheaper; where types are only known dynamically, Any::downcast_ref offers a runtime-checked alternative with no visitor trait at all.
pitfalls: Adding an element type is a breaking change for every Visitor implementation: plan a default method or an Any fallback if the set may grow.
Trait objects need indirection (Box/Vec<Box<dyn Shape>>) and cannot have generic methods, so a generic visit<T> is not available on dyn Visitor.
The visitor holds &mut state while elements are borrowed, which makes borrow-checker conflicts common: keep traversal state in one place.
